original_question: Is a flexibly permutation-stable group always permutation-stable?
target_in_paper: Problem 21.85 in the section "New Problems (21st issue, 2026)": "Is a flexibly permutation-stable group always permutation-stable?"
correct_elements: Your draft captures the exact official open problem in the paper, essentially verbatim, and it has the right logical direction: whether flexible permutation stability implies permutation stability. It also stays narrowly focused on the specific question asked in the paper, rather than drifting to the neighboring question about SL_n(Z).
missing_details: In the paper, these notions are stated only for a finitely generated group G; that hypothesis is implicit in your draft and should be made explicit.
The paper defines permutation stability using the normalized Hamming distance d_n(σ,τ)=(1/n)|{x in {1,...,n} : σ(x) != τ(x)}| on S_n; your draft does not supply this metric.
The term almost-homomorphism must be defined: it is a sequence of set-theoretic maps f_n:G->S_n such that d_n(f_n(g)f_n(h),f_n(gh))->0 as n->infinity for all g,h in G.
The term close to a homomorphism must be defined: there must exist homomorphisms ρ_n:G->S_n with d_n(ρ_n(g),f_n(g))->0 as n->infinity for all g in G.
The paper defines flexible permutation stability via the flexible distance d_n^flex, and that definition is missing from your draft.
The flexible distance is d_n^flex(α,β)=(1/n)(|{x in {1,...,n} : α(x) != β(x)}|+(m-n)) for α in S_n and β in S_m with n<=m; this must be stated to make the question stand-alone.
Flexible closeness allows approximation by homomorphisms ρ_n:G->S_{m_n} into larger symmetric groups, with integers m_n>=n; your draft does not mention the larger target groups or the sequence m_n.
The quantifiers are pointwise in the group elements: the limits are required for every g,h in G and every g in G as n->infinity, not merely on a generating set or uniformly over finite subsets.
The draft does not indicate that the question compares two paper-defined properties and therefore needs the exact local notation from Problems 21.83 and 21.84 to be interpretable on its own.
refined_question: Let G be a finitely generated group. For σ,τ in S_n, define d_n(σ,τ)=(1/n)|{x in {1,...,n} : σ(x) != τ(x)}|. A sequence of set-theoretic maps f_n:G->S_n is called an almost-homomorphism if d_n(f_n(g)f_n(h),f_n(gh))->0 as n->infinity for every g,h in G. The group G is called permutation-stable if for every almost-homomorphism {f_n} there exists a sequence of group homomorphisms ρ_n:G->S_n such that d_n(ρ_n(g),f_n(g))->0 as n->infinity for every g in G. For α in S_n and β in S_m with n<=m, define d_n^flex(α,β)=(1/n)(|{x in {1,...,n} : α(x) != β(x)}|+(m-n)). The group G is called flexibly permutation-stable if for every almost-homomorphism {f_n} there exist integers m_n>=n and group homomorphisms ρ_n:G->S_{m_n} such that d_n^flex(f_n(g),ρ_n(g))->0 as n->infinity for every g in G. Must every finitely generated flexibly permutation-stable group be permutation-stable?
justification: The nearest official target is exactly Problem 21.85. However, that question is not self-contained unless one imports the definitions given immediately before it: Problem 21.83 defines d_n, almost-homomorphism, closeness to a homomorphism, and permutation stability; Problem 21.84 defines d_n^flex, flexible closeness, and flexible permutation stability. Those nearby items also impose the finitely generated hypothesis on G and specify the relevant quantifiers as limits holding for all g,h in G or all g in G as n tends to infinity. No separate equivalent reformulation is stated there, so the sharp paper-faithful rewrite is simply the same implication question with all of 21.83-21.84 unfolded.
